title: A tensor power has a square difference from the parameter base over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $X_i\to S$ for $i=1,2,3$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] that are smooth separated morphisms of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume each $X_i$ is geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], meaning integral after every field extension. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Put $C=X_1\times_SX_2\times_SX_3$, $P=X_1\times_SX_1\times_SX_2\times_SX_2$, and $\pi:P\times_SX_3\to P$. At coordinates $(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1,z)$ write $r_{ab}(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1,z)=(x_a,y_b,z)$ for $a,b\in\{0,1\}$. For an invertible module $A$ on $C$, define its square difference by $$D(A)=r_{00}^*A\otimes r_{11}^*A\otimes(r_{01}^*A)^{-1}\otimes(r_{10}^*A)^{-1}.$$ Here inverse means the dual invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], and all products, pullbacks and tensors are those of [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every invertible $A$ on $C$ there are an integer $n\geq1$ and an invertible module $N$ on $P$ such that $$D(A^{\otimes n})\cong\pi^*N.$$

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.2(ii), field case, specialized to smooth separated finite-presentation geometrically integral factors; March 31, 2026 author version, printed pp.11-12, read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the finite-extension square lemma to the given $k$, the three smooth separated finite-presentation geometrically integral factors, and $A$. It gives a finite extension $K/k$, an invertible $N_K$ on $P_K$, and an isomorphism $D(A_K)\cong\pi_K^*N_K$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2(ii), Claim 5.2.1 and its first application, pp.11-12

proof.text: Let $d=[K:k]$. The Picard norm for the finite field extension, applied to $Z=P$ and to $Z=P\times_kX_3$, commutes with arbitrary pullback and sends the pullback of an invertible module to its $d$-fold tensor power. Pullback and tensor product commute with the four maps $r_{ab}$, so the pullback of $D(A)$ to $K$ is canonically $D(A_K)$; expanding the four factors also gives $D(A^{\otimes d})\cong D(A)^{\otimes d}$.

source.place: Tags 0BCY and 0BD2, together with the tensor/pullback identities in the square-difference definition

proof.text: Apply the norm to the isomorphism from Step 1. Naturality for $\pi$ gives $\operatorname{Nm}(D(A_K))\cong\pi^*\operatorname{Nm}(N_K)$. By Step 2, the left side is $D(A)^{\otimes d}$, hence isomorphic to $D(A^{\otimes d})$. Taking $n=d\geq1$ and $N=\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,P}(N_K)$ proves the required assertion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_fieldProductSquare_tensorPower (k : Type u) [Field k] (X₁ X₂ X₃ : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [Smooth X₁.hom] [Smooth X₂.hom] [Smooth X₃.hom] [IsSeparated X₁.hom] [IsSeparated X₂.hom] [IsSeparated X₃.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation X₁.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation X₂.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation X₃.hom] [QuasiCompact X₁.hom] [QuasiCompact X₂.hom] [QuasiCompact X₃.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral X₁.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral X₂.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral X₃.hom] : let C := (X₁ ⨯ X₂) ⨯ X₃ let P := (X₁ ⨯ X₁) ⨯ (X₂ ⨯ X₂) let Q := P ⨯ X₃ let x (a : Bool) : Q ⟶ X₁ := prod.fst ≫ prod.fst ≫ (if a then prod.snd else prod.fst) let y (b : Bool) : Q ⟶ X₂ := prod.fst ≫ prod.snd ≫ (if b then prod.snd else prod.fst) let r (a b : Bool) : Q ⟶ C := prod.lift (prod.lift (x a) (y b)) prod.snd let D (M : C.left.Modules) : Q.left.Modules := (((tensorPullback (r false false).left).obj M ⊗ (tensorPullback (r true true).left).obj M) ⊗ dual ((tensorPullback (r false true).left).obj M)) ⊗ dual ((tensorPullback (r true false).left).obj M) ∀ (A : C.left.Modules), A.IsInvertible → ∃ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n ∧ ∃ (N : P.left.Modules), N.IsInvertible ∧ Nonempty (D (A.tensorPow n) ≅ (tensorPullback (prod.fst : Q ⟶ P).left).obj N)
